title: Value each start, and the risk it removes

blocks.text: Problem statement
Finance and the asset team both had comments on the step-03 plan:

Finance: you value every project at its earliest-start NPV, whatever year you start it. A project started in 2030 is worth less than the same project started in 2027; we sent you the NPV for every start year. Use it.
Asset management: NPV is not why we replace old equipment. Each project lowers the failure risk of one asset. We want to see how much risk a plan removes, and a plan that removes the most of it.

You start from the rule-keeping planner of the lesson before. Price every start: its NPV is the figure finance quotes for that start year, and the risk it removes is the asset's yearly risk, failure probability times the cost of a failure, over every year after the work ends to the end of the plan. The failure probability comes from the asset's Weibull curve. The export says which of the two the plan maximizes, NPV unless it says risk, and the plan and its report carry both.
The export gives each asset's `age` in the plan's first year; the asset is one year older in each later year. The report changes in three ways, every amount with thousands commas:

items: the funded line keeps its form, `funded <n> of <all> projects, capex $<capex>k of $<budgets>k, value $<value>k`, but its value is now the plan's objective, what the model maximized, in whole $k (the NPV of the actual starts when the export asks for NPV);
a new line follows it: `NPV $<npv>k, risk reduced $<risk>k (maximized: <objective>)`, NPV in whole $k and risk with one decimal;
each funded project's line ends `capex <capex>  npv <npv>  <name>`: the label `npv` replaces `value`, and the amount, right-aligned in 6 characters, is the NPV of the year the project starts.

blocks.text: `cipt/goals.py` is the next lesson's stub, as the reference has it; no code of this step imports it, so leave it as it is.

Run executes `main.py`, which plans the demo export and prints the report; `expected/report.txt` is the report it should print. Submit runs every test in `tests/`, the earlier steps' included, and compares Run's report with the expected one.
Blueprint
Write each method below. The tests check each one by itself and the whole program end to end, so you may change any other part of the code as you see fit.
`annual_pof` in `cipt/value.py`
def annual_pof(beta: float, eta: float, age: float) -> float

items: **Contract.** Returns the chance that an asset of this age fails within the next year, given that it has not failed yet, on a Weibull curve with shape beta and scale eta.
**Modeling idea.** The conditional one-year PoF is 1 - exp(H(age) - H(age + 1)), with the cumulative hazard H(a) = (a / eta) ** beta.

**Taught in** [7.3.1 Probability of Failure and Hazard Curves (Weibull)](../../../../07-the-capital-planning-domain/32-asset-risk/units/unit-01/7.3.1-probability-of-failure-and-hazard-curves-weibull.unit.html).

blocks.text: `annual_risk` in `cipt/value.py`
def annual_risk(request: Request, project: Project, year: int) -> float

items: **Contract.** Returns the expected failure cost, in $k, of the project's asset in a calendar year if nothing is done: the consequence of failure times the PoF at the asset's age in that year. The export's age is the asset's age in the plan's first year, so in year y the age is age + y - first year.
**Modeling idea.** Risk is PoF times CoF, and the age grows by one each year from the plan's first year.
**Taught in** [7.3.3 Consequence of Failure and Risk = PoF × CoF](../../../../07-the-capital-planning-domain/32-asset-risk/units/unit-03/7.3.3-consequence-of-failure-and-risk-pof-cof.unit.html).

blocks.text: `risk_reduction` in `cipt/value.py`
def risk_reduction(request: Request, project: Project, start: int) -> float

items: **Contract.** Returns the risk removed by a start in a given year: the asset's annual risk summed over every year after the work ends, to the plan's last year.
**Modeling idea.** Work removes the risk of the years after it is done; a later start removes fewer years.

**Taught in** [7.3.4 Risk Reduction From an Intervention, Year by Year](../../../../07-the-capital-planning-domain/32-asset-risk/units/unit-04/7.3.4-risk-reduction-from-an-intervention-year-by-year.unit.html).

blocks.text: `coefficients` in `cipt/value.py`
def coefficients(request: Request) -> dict[tuple[str, int], tuple[int, float]]

items: **Contract.** Returns, for every project and start year the model has a variable for, the pair (NPV of that start, risk reduction of that start).
**Modeling idea.** Price each start before the model is built, so each variable gets its own coefficient.

**Taught in** [7.2.4 Precomputing NPV Coefficients by Start Year](../../../../07-the-capital-planning-domain/31-financial-evaluation/units/unit-04/7.2.4-precomputing-npv-coefficients-by-start-year.unit.html).

blocks.text: `build` in `cipt/model.py`
def build(request: Request) -> Built

items: **Contract.** Keeps the plan's NPV and its risk removed as two expressions on the Built, and maximizes the one the request's objective names ('npv' or 'risk').
**Modeling idea.** Two measures over the same variables are two linear expressions; the objective picks one.

**Taught in** [14.2.4 Value: NPV by Start Year and Risk Reduction](../../../../14-growing-real-projects/55-project-cipt-planner/units/unit-04/14.2.4-value-npv-by-start-year-and-risk-reduction.unit.html).

blocks.text: `read_plan` in `cipt/solve.py`
def read_plan(built: Built, result: mathopt.SolveResult) -> Plan

items: **Contract.** Also returns the plan's NPV and risk removed, evaluated from the two expressions at the solution.
**Modeling idea.** The plan reports both measures whichever one was maximized.

**Taught in** [4.2.2 Reading `SolveResult`: Termination, Primal and Dual Solutions, Statistics](../../../../04-google-or-tools-in-depth/13-mathopt-core/units/unit-02/4.2.2-reading-solveresult-termination-primal-and-dual-solutions-statistics.unit.html).

blocks.text: `load_request` in `cipt/data.py`
def load_request(raw: dict) -> Request

items: **Contract.** Also reads each project's NPV for every start year and its asset (id, age, Weibull shape and scale, consequence of failure), and the request's objective, 'npv' by default; refuses any other objective.
**Modeling idea.** The export already carries NPV by start year and asset health; read them where they are.

**Taught in** [7.2.4 Precomputing NPV Coefficients by Start Year](../../../../07-the-capital-planning-domain/31-financial-evaluation/units/unit-04/7.2.4-precomputing-npv-coefficients-by-start-year.unit.html).

blocks.text: `render` in `cipt/report.py`
def render(request: Request, plan: Plan) -> str

items: **Contract.** Changes the report in three ways. The funded line's `value $<value>k` is now the plan's objective, what the model maximized (the NPV of the actual starts when the objective is 'npv'). After it comes the line `NPV $<npv>k, risk reduced $<risk>k (maximized: <objective>)`, NPV in whole $k and risk with one decimal, both with thousands commas. Each funded project's line shows `npv` and the NPV of the year the project starts, right-aligned in 6 characters, where it showed `value` and the earliest-start value.
**Modeling idea.** A report shows the measure that was not maximized as well as the one that was.

**Taught in** [14.2.4 Value: NPV by Start Year and Risk Reduction](../../../../14-growing-real-projects/55-project-cipt-planner/units/unit-04/14.2.4-value-npv-by-start-year-and-risk-reduction.unit.html).

"""A plan: what the solve decided, in the planners' terms."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Plan:
    """The answer to a request.

    `status` is "optimal", "infeasible" or another solver outcome in lower case; `starts` maps each
    funded project to the year its work starts; `objective` is what the model maximized; `npv` and
    `risk` are the plan's NPV and the risk it removes, both in $k, whichever was maximized.
    """

    status: str
    starts: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
    objective: float = 0.0
    npv: float = 0.0
    risk: float = 0.0

    @property
    def funded(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        return tuple(sorted(self.starts))

File: cipt/solve.py

"""Solve a request with HiGHS and read the answer back as a Plan."""

from __future__ import annotations

import ctypes
import os
import sys

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt
from ortools.math_opt.solvers import highs_pb2

from .data import Request
from .model import Built, build
from .plan import Plan

#: One thread, set in HiGHS's own options; the first HiGHS solve of a process fixes the count.
PARAMS = mathopt.SolveParameters(highs=highs_pb2.HighsOptionsProto(int_options={"threads": 1}))


def run_highs(model: mathopt.Model) -> mathopt.SolveResult:
    """Solve with stdout pointed at /dev/null, so HiGHS's stray C output stays out of reports."""
    sys.stdout.flush()
    saved, sink = os.dup(1), os.open(os.devnull, os.O_WRONLY)
    os.dup2(sink, 1)
    try:
        return mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS, params=PARAMS)
    finally:
        ctypes.CDLL(None).fflush(None)
        os.dup2(saved, 1)
        os.close(saved)
        os.close(sink)


def read_plan(built: Built, result: mathopt.SolveResult) -> Plan:
    """Turn a solver result into a Plan: each funded project with the year its x is 1."""
    status = result.termination.reason.name.lower()
    if not result.has_primal_feasible_solution():
        return Plan(status=status)
    values = result.variable_values()
    starts = {pid: t for (pid, t), var in built.x.items() if values[var] > 0.5}
    return Plan(status=status, starts=starts, objective=result.objective_value(),
                npv=mathopt.evaluate_expression(built.npv, values),
                risk=mathopt.evaluate_expression(built.risk, values))


def solve(request: Request) -> Plan:
    built = build(request)
    return read_plan(built, run_highs(built.model))
